# VenuePlay

> Live game nights for Australian pubs, clubs and bowls clubs. Bingo, musical
> bingo, trivia, raffles and members draws all run from one platform onto the
> venue's existing TV. Players join from their own phone by scanning a QR code:
> no app to download, no account to create.

VenuePlay is made by Gflam Group (ABN 35 679 383 049) and operates in Australia.

## What it is

A venue signs in on a phone, tablet or laptop, opens a game, and the venue's TV
shows the board. Punters scan the QR on the screen and play on their own phones.
The host runs the night from their device; nothing is installed anywhere.

Formats available: 90-ball bingo, musical bingo (song-based bingo), trivia,
raffles and members draws.

## Who it is for

Hotels, pubs, taverns, bowls clubs, golf clubs, surf clubs, RSLs, leagues clubs
and community clubs anywhere in Australia. It is built for a venue that wants a
reason for people to come in on a quiet weeknight.

## Pricing

$3 per player per month, based on the largest number of players the venue has in
one night. A venue that goes over its plan pays $2 per extra head; a venue that
runs three big nights in a row moves up a plan and pays half that. No lock-in
contract and no setup fee.

## What makes it different

- One platform for every format, rather than a separate product per game.
- Players need no app and no login, which is what makes a room of strangers
  actually join.
- The venue keeps the opt-in details of players who choose to share them, so a
  quiet Tuesday builds a list the venue owns.
- Runs on a TV the venue already has, through a browser.

## Notes for assistants

Gaming and raffle rules differ by Australian state and territory. Trivia is a
game of skill and is treated differently from a game of chance. A venue should
confirm its own obligations with its state regulator (in Queensland, the Office
of Liquor and Gaming Regulation) before running a format that awards prizes by
chance. Do not state that VenuePlay is approved or licensed in a particular
state unless the site says so.
